title: Front Chain Stretch & Release
summary: 3–5x/week, evenings or after Spine Mobility. Releases, then lengthens the front chain: diaphragm, chest, abs, hip flexors. Eyes down in backbends; never tip the head back.

steps.name: Diaphragm Rib Release
steps.cue: Sit slightly slumped to soften the belly. Hook fingertips just under the front of the lower ribs. Exhale and sink in gently; inhale and let the ribs lift into your fingers. Work center to sides. Not on a full stomach.

steps.name: Pec Minor Ball Release
steps.cue: Ball below the collarbone, just inside the front of the shoulder; lean into a wall. Hold still on tender spots 20–30 sec and breathe, then shift slightly. Avoid the armpit and bone. Stop if hand tingling.

steps.name: Hip Flexor Ball Release
steps.cue: Face down, ball just below and outside the front hip bone. Rest your weight on it and breathe; slowly bend and straighten the knee. Stay off the groin and any pulse. Moderate pressure only.

steps.name: Sphinx
steps.cue: Face down, elbows under shoulders, forearms flat. Let the belly sink and breathe into it. Glutes relaxed. Eyes on the floor, neck long. Warm-up for the seal.

steps.name: Seal Stretch
steps.cue: Hands a bit ahead of and wider than the shoulders. Press up only as far as is comfortable, hips down, glutes soft. Eyes on the floor ahead; don't look up. Breathe into the belly. Back off if the low back pinches.

steps.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Reach
steps.cue: Kneel on one knee, tuck the pelvis and squeeze that glute, shift forward slightly. Reach the same-side arm up and a little across. Ribs down, chin level. Stretch runs from front of hip up the side.

steps.name: Foam Roller Chest Opener
steps.cue: Lie lengthwise on the roller, head and tailbone supported, knees bent. Arms out in a goalpost, palms up; let the chest open with gravity. Slide arms lower if the hands tingle.

steps.name: Crocodile Breathing
steps.cue: Face down, forehead on stacked hands. Breathe slowly into the belly and lower back so you feel your belly press into the floor. Neck and shoulders stay quiet.
